verses.text: Then Solomon said, "The LORD said he would live in thick darkness.
And I've built you a house to call home, a place where you can live forever."
The king turned to face the whole assembly of Israel and blessed them as they stood.
He said, "Praise the LORD, the God of Israel. He kept with his own hands the promise he spoke to my father David:
'Since the day I brought my people out of Egypt, I hadn't chosen any city from Israel's tribes for a house to bear my name, or anyone to rule over my people Israel.
Now I've chosen Jerusalem for my name to be there, and I've chosen David to lead my people Israel.'
My father David wanted to build a house to honor the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
The LORD told my father, 'It was good that you wanted to build a house to honor my name.
But your own son will be the one to build the house for my name.'
The LORD has done what he promised. I've succeeded my father David and taken Israel's throne, as the LORD said, and I've built the house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
I've placed the ark there. It holds the covenant the LORD made with the Israelites."
Solomon stood in front of the LORD's altar before the whole assembly of Israel and spread out his hands.

He had made a bronze platform five cubits long, five cubits wide, and three cubits high and set it in the middle of the courtyard. He stood on it, then knelt in front of the whole assembly and stretched his hands toward heaven.
He said, "LORD, God of Israel, there is no god like you in heaven or on earth. You keep your covenant and show faithful love to your servants who live before you wholeheartedly.
You kept the promise you made to your servant David, my father. You spoke it with your mouth, and what we see today you fulfilled with your hand.

Now, LORD, God of Israel, keep this promise to your servant David, my father: 'You will always have a descendant before me on Israel's throne, as long as your children pay attention to how they live and follow my law as you have lived before me.'
Now, LORD, God of Israel, let the word you spoke to your servant David come true.
Will God really live here on earth with people? Even the highest heavens can't hold you, much less this house I've built.
Still, LORD my God, pay attention to your servant's prayer and plea. Listen to the cry and prayer I'm bringing before you.
Keep your eyes on this house day and night, on the place where you said you would put your name. Hear the prayers your servant makes toward this place.
Hear the pleas of your servant and your people Israel when they pray toward this place. Hear them from your home in heaven, and when you hear, forgive.
If someone wrongs a neighbor and is required to swear an oath, and they come before your altar in this house to swear it,
hear from heaven and act. Judge between your servants, making the guilty answer for what they've done and giving the innocent the justice they deserve.
If your people Israel are defeated by an enemy because they've sinned against you, and they turn back, confess your name, and pray and plead before you in this house,
hear from heaven, forgive your people Israel's sin, and bring them back to the land you gave them and their ancestors.
When the sky shuts and there is no rain because they've sinned against you, if they pray toward this place, confess your name, and turn from their sin when you discipline them,
hear in heaven and forgive the sin of your servants, your people Israel. Teach them the good way to live and send rain on the land you gave your people as their inheritance.
If famine or disease strikes the land, or blight, mildew, locusts, or caterpillars come, or enemies surround their cities, whatever plague or sickness comes,
hear any prayer or plea from one person or from all your people Israel. Each one knows their own pain and trouble, and they spread their hands toward this house.
Hear from heaven, where you live, and forgive. Give each person what their conduct deserves, for you know their heart. You alone know every human heart.
Then they'll honor you with reverence and live in your ways as long as they live in the land you gave our ancestors.
As for a foreigner who doesn't belong to your people Israel, when they come from a distant country because of your great name, your mighty hand, and your outstretched arm, and pray toward this house,
hear from your home in heaven and do what they ask, so all the peoples of the earth may know your name and revere you as Israel does. Let them know this house I've built bears your name.
When your people go out to fight their enemies wherever you send them and pray toward this city you've chosen and this house I've built for your name,
hear their prayers and pleas from heaven, and uphold their cause.
If they sin against you, as everyone does, and in your anger you give them over to enemies who take them captive to a land far away or nearby,
and they come to their senses in the land where they're held captive and turn back and plead with you there, saying, 'We've sinned, we've done wrong, and we've acted wickedly,'
if they return to you with all their heart and soul in the land of their captivity, and pray toward the land you gave their ancestors, the city you've chosen, and the house I've built for your name,
hear their prayers and pleas from your dwelling in heaven. Uphold their cause, and forgive your people who have sinned against you.
Now, my God, please keep your eyes open and your ears attentive to the prayers made in this place.
Rise, LORD God, and come to your resting place, you and the ark of your strength. LORD God, may your priests be clothed with salvation, and may your faithful people rejoice in your goodness.
LORD God, please welcome the one you've anointed. Remember the faithful love you showed David your servant."
